name: Cardiac Sarcoidosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Japanese Ministry of Health and Welfare Criteria for Cardiac Sarcoidosis

criteria.description: High-grade atrioventricular block or ventricular tachycardia
Positive cardiac MRI or FDG-PET showing myocardial inflammation or scarring
Histological or clinical evidence of sarcoidosis in other organs
ECG abnormalities such as bundle branch block or premature ventricular contractions

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Either histological confirmation from myocardial tissue or a combination of clinical, imaging, and extracardiac sarcoidosis evidence as per formal criteria
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Endomyocardial biopsy has low sensitivity; diagnosis often relies on clinical and imaging criteria combined with extracardiac sarcoidosis.

occasional.symptomName: Palpitations due to premature ventricular contractions

imaging: Cardiac MRI showing late gadolinium enhancement and myocardial edema
FDG-PET scan demonstrating active myocardial inflammation
Echocardiography showing regional wall motion abnormalities or ventricular dysfunction
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; familial clustering reported in some cases
other: Endomyocardial biopsy demonstrating non-caseating granulomas (low sensitivity)
ECG abnormalities including bundle branch block and ventricular arrhythmias

distinguishingFeatures: Poor response to standard sarcoidosis treatments
Coronary artery disease evidence on angiography

redFlags: New onset high-grade atrioventricular block in young or middle-aged adults
Unexplained ventricular tachycardia or ventricular fibrillation
references: Birnie DH, et al. Cardiac Sarcoidosis. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2020;75(12):1423-1434.
Hiraga H, et al. Diagnostic criteria for cardiac sarcoidosis. Jpn Cir J. 1993;57(9):845-853.
Sekiguchi M, et al. Cardiac sarcoidosis: diagnosis and treatment. Curr Cardiol Rep. 2019;21(10):111.
